target_customer: US brands (initially apparel and textile) importing from overseas factories, starting with Indonesia
problem: US brands lose money to ghost suppliers, hidden fees and missed deadlines, and the reliable factories sit behind long-standing personal relationships outsiders cannot access.
business_model: Sourcing brokerage (commission per deal, assumed from description; vendor financing also mentioned) with AI-assisted human brokers
product_category: AI-enabled cross-border sourcing broker / global trade marketplace

founders.name: Edward Haryono
founders.background_notes: Grew up in Indonesia; family has about 50 years in retail and logistics; president of nonprofit IABA-PNW.

founders.name: Jennifer Prasetyo
founders.background_notes: Family has 50+ years in Indonesian textile manufacturing; runs the @jenandtech channel with a large following.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly workflow software layered on human brokers; the difficulty is in supply-side relationships and operations rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Founders' family relationships with Indonesian factories are hard for outsiders to replicate, but this is a relationship moat held by a two-person team, and the software layer is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet observable; company is in the Spring 2026 batch.

market_need_then: Company cites about $3T of US goods imports a year and complaints about ghost suppliers and hidden fees; it reports sourcing $900K+ for 40+ brands in about 5 months (company-reported, via a search summary of an aggregator page).
outcome_analysis: Saudara AI is a two-person Spring 2026 company with an aggregator-reported $500K pre-seed and company-claimed early GMV, so there is no outcome to explain yet. Its distinguishing feature is founder-market fit through family ties to Indonesian textile manufacturing, but the sources provide no independent traction or competition evidence.
